# Novanta Inc. (NOVT) — Munger/Buffett Read

## Circle of Competence
Novanta makes precision photonics, medical motion-control components, and machine-vision systems that get engineered into other companies' products — surgical robots, industrial lasers, automation lines. This is an understandable business at the level that matters: it's a component/sub-system supplier selling into OEM design cycles, not a black-box technology story. Moderately inside the circle — graspable, though the depth of any single end-market (e.g., surgical robotics) would need real homework before sizing a position.

## Moat & Durability — Score: 6/10
The moat here is design-win stickiness: once a Novanta component is qualified into a customer's regulated or safety-critical system (a surgical robot, an industrial laser), swapping suppliers means re-qualification, which is slow and costly for the customer. That buys multi-year revenue visibility and some pricing power. But gross margin (44.5%) and operating margin (11.5%) are solid-industrial, not fortress-like, and the space has credible larger competitors. This is a durable niche position, not a dominant moat that obviously holds for a decade without erosion.

## Management & Capital Allocation
The packet has no direct data on insider ownership, management tenure, buybacks, or dividend policy — a genuine blind spot, not a judgment. What the reported numbers imply is mixed at best: ROE of 5.1% is weak, and it's weak *despite* elevated leverage (debt/equity 17.7x by this packet's measure) — leverage that isn't showing up as amplified shareholder returns. The 105x trailing vs. 38.7x forward P/E gap is large enough to suggest either one-time charges depressed this year's reported earnings, or consensus is underwriting a big earnings recovery. Either way, this needs verification in the filings before trusting the capital-allocation story implied by consensus estimates.

## Predictability
10.3% revenue growth is a decent single data point, but one quarter's snapshot doesn't establish the kind of quiet, multi-year earnings consistency that makes a decision 'easy' in Munger's sense. The trailing/forward P/E gap reads as earnings volatility rather than steady compounding. Momentum data compounds the caution: RSI of 71 (overbought), price 24% above the 200-day moving average, and a 46% trailing-12-month return describe a stock in a momentum regime, not a business quietly proving out its economics. Net: below-average predictability, driven partly by real information gaps in this packet.

## Inversion — How the Owner Loses Money From Here
1. **Multiple compression**: at 105x trailing / 38.7x forward earnings and 32.4x EV/EBITDA, any growth deceleration re-rates the stock sharply even if operations hold up.
2. **Thin ROE meets leverage**: 5.1% ROE next to elevated debt/equity leaves little cushion — margin pressure or a goodwill impairment from past M&A could push returns on capital lower still.
3. **Cyclical demand air pocket**: robotics/automation and medical-device capex are cyclical end markets; a demand pause, combined with 17.2% of float already sold short (8.7 days to cover) and an overbought technical setup (RSI 71, +24% vs. 200dma), sets up a fast unwind if growth disappoints.

## Valuation — Owner Earnings
The packet doesn't give a share price or count directly, but market cap ($6.29B) against Novanta's roughly ~35-36M shares implies a current price near the $175-180 area — consistent with the momentum data showing the stock up 46% over the trailing year. FCF yield of 1.88% implies roughly $118M of trailing free cash flow, or about $3.30/share; the much higher forward P/E-implied EPS (~$4.50) suggests normalized earning power somewhat above trailing FCF once one-time items roll off.

Using a blended normalized owner-earnings estimate of ~$4.20/share, a 5-year growth assumption tapering from 8% to a 3% terminal rate, and an 10-11% discount rate (reflecting the stock's above-market beta of 1.68 and moderate, not exceptional, moat), a two-stage DCF lands intrinsic value in the **$65-$95/share range**. Against an implied current price near $176, that's a margin of safety of roughly **-50% to -60%** — the stock is priced for a materially better business than the fundamentals (5.1% ROE, 11.5% op margin, 10.3% growth) currently support. A fair-value FCF yield for this quality of business is closer to 5-6% (17-20x FCF); the market is pricing it at roughly 1.9% (53x FCF).

## The Cloning Caveat
Two superinvestors initiated NOVT positions this quarter, but neither is a high-conviction signal. Torray Funds sized its new stake at just 0.27% of portfolio, and Polen Capital Management's new position is a token 0.02% — essentially a research-sized nibble, not a concentrated bet. Compare that to what a 20-40%-of-portfolio position from a focused manager would mean: real corroboration of a thesis. Here, both buys read as managers testing the name at the margin, which is weak corroboration at best and shouldn't be treated as validating the valuation.

## Verdict
**Pass**, conviction 2/10. The business is understandable and has a real, if moderate, moat, but management quality/capital allocation can't be verified from this packet, predictability is below par, and the price demands a far better business than the fundamentals show. Munger's default answer applies: no.
momentum_thesis: NOVT's 12-month uptrend is accelerating, not aging — the 22.1% three-month return accounts for nearly all of the 24.8% six-month move, and the stock is running at RSI 71.4 and 23.9% above its 200DMA, deep into technically extended territory. Short interest at 17.2% of float with 8.7 days to cover is unusually heavy for a $6.3B name and, paired with a lopsided 0.10 put/call OI ratio, points to a live squeeze dynamic rather than a bearish crowd — shorts are being run over, not confirmed. Torray Funds and Polen Capital both initiated new positions in Q2 2026, but at 0.27% and 0.02% of portfolio these are toe-in-the-water allocations, not conviction stakes, and share counts aren't disclosed, so the smart-money signal is directional confirmation at best, not a thesis driver. Valuation has decoupled from fundamentals — 105.3x trailing earnings, 38.7x forward, 5.1% ROE, 1.9% FCF yield — meaning the move is being carried entirely by price momentum and short-covering rather than earnings support. At 1.68 beta, any macro wobble or earnings disappointment removes the squeeze bid quickly, and the thin put open interest means there is little built-in hedge already in place to cushion an unwind.
